questions: Did kd 0.8 keep the s-bend off-track exits at 1 of 20 or fewer and raise the score above 703.8?
Did steering_oscillation stay below about 0.4 on the oval and s-bend with kd 0.8?
Did slalom line_loss_events or off-track count change from about 1.2 and 20 of 20?
Is noise_robustness on the s-bend and oval reported in a way that suggests the geometry handles the sensor noise margin well?

intent: Hold the best measured geometry (wheel_track 0.16, sensors at y 0.08 with 16 mm footprints on the ±0.024 m span) so that the Integrator's controller tests, kd 0.8 and any kp change, are compared on a fixed platform. Do not widen the span, change the footprint or change the track width. Expected result: s-bend off-track exits at 1 of 20 or fewer, and an oval finish of 20 of 20, which keeps the robot robust for the unseen final track.
learning: Track width is settled at 0.16 at this sensor layout: 0.17 raised s-bend exits, and 0.10 and 0.12 were both worse. Slalom is not moved by track width, span, footprint or lookahead, so the remaining levers are controller damping and, if needed, a separate slalom test after this race.
rationale: The race data points to one stable geometry. Track width at sensor y 0.08 with 16 mm footprints and a ±0.024 m span rose monotonically from 0.10 to 0.16 (496.4, 561.6, 628.6, 661.5). At 0.17 the score fell to 651.1 as s-bend off-track exits rose from 1 to 2, so the gain has peaked at 0.16. Iteration 10 (wheel_track 0.16, kp 4.0, kd 0.5) scored 703.8, the best so far, with the s-bend finishing 20 of 20 and the oval 20 of 20. Slalom is still 0 of 20 at every geometry tested, with line_loss about 1.2 to 1.4 and max_error about 0.065. Span, footprint and lookahead have each been tested without fixing it, and span widening (iteration 2) and a 12 mm footprint (iteration 0) both did worse. The final race runs on an unseen track, so a robust, measured geometry is worth more than a speculative change. I am therefore holding the geometry at the best measured values (wheel_track 0.16, y 0.08, 16 mm footprints, x ±0.024 at 12 mm pitch, body, wheels and mass unchanged). The Integrator's kd 0.8 test is a controller change and stays with them. Expected result: the same geometry behaviour as iteration 10, so the controller test isolates damping.
